setup.players: Four players. Partnerships formed through king-calling in appropriate contracts, or one player alone in solo contracts.
setup.deck: 54-card Austrian Tarock pack: 22 trumps (Tarocks numbered I-XXI plus the SkÃ¼s), and 8 cards in each of four suits (Clubs, Spades, Hearts, Diamonds).
setup.dealing: Standard KÃ¶nigrufen dealing: 12 cards to each player, 6 cards to the talon. Dealt in packets of 6 anticlockwise, starting with player to dealer's right. Play proceeds anticlockwise.

rules.objective: In positive contracts, the declarer's side must take at least 36 of the 70 available card points. Negative contracts have objectives like losing all tricks or winning an exact number of tricks.
rules.gameplay: Deal 12 cards each and 6 to talon. Auction to determine declarer and contract. In king-calling contracts declarer names a suit; holder of that king is partner (hidden until king is played). Declarer may exchange with talon in some contracts. Announcements (bonuses, kontra) then play. Follow suit; must trump if unable. Highest trump or highest of led suit wins trick. Count card points; declarer's side needs 36+ in positive contracts.
keyRules: Deal 12 cards each, 6 to talon; deal in two packets of 6 anticlockwise from dealer's right.
Auction to determine declarer; forehand may say Mein Spiel; three consecutive passes end bidding.
In Rufer/Solo/Besserrufer declarer calls a king of a suit; that king's holder is partner (hidden until played).
Follow suit; if unable, must play a trump. Highest trump or highest of led suit wins trick.
Positive contracts: declarer's side needs 36+ of 70 card points. Negative: lose every trick, or take exactly one or two tricks, or fewest points.
Bonuses (Trull, Pagat Ultimo, Valat, etc.) and kontra/rekontra double scores; announcements before play.

strategy.basic: In positive contracts, focus on capturing high-value cards. The 5-point cards (kings, SkÃ¼s, XXI, I) are the most important. Try to win tricks containing these cards.
strategy.intermediate: When exchanging with the talon, evaluate both packets carefully. Look for packets containing kings or high trumps. When calling a king, choose a suit where you need help.
strategy.advanced: Master the timing of announcements. Announcing a bonus (like Pagat Ultimo) doubles its value but commits you to achieving it. Calculate whether the risk is worth the reward. In negative contracts, the strategy reverses - you must carefully control your trick-taking.
tips: Keep track of which trumps have been played, especially the high ones (SkÃ¼s, XXI).
In Rufer, your partner is hidden until the called king appears - play accordingly.
Don't overbid - it's better to pass and defend than to declare a contract you can't make.
The Mond (XXI) is vulnerable to the SkÃ¼s - be cautious when playing it.

difficulty.medium: Reasonable bidding and talon selection. Basic card tracking. Understands partner play in Rufer.

trumpConfig.trumpSuitRanking: Sküs highest then XXI down to I
trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Highest trump wins trick; must follow suit then must trump if unable.

trickConfig.leadRestrictions: Forehand leads first trick in positive contracts; declarer leads in negative.

edgeCases.text: Called king in talon: declarer plays alone against three; talon added to declarer's tricks.
Emperor trick (optional): if Sküs, XXI and I are in same trick, Pagat wins that trick.
Besserrufer: if called king in talon, declarer may play on or give up hand for 3 points.
Negative contracts: must beat highest card on table if possible; Pagat only when last trump.

customActions.description: Place six cards from the deal into the talon (middle). Dealt in packets: first 6 to each player, then 6 to talon, then 6 more to each player.
Name a suit; the holder of the king of that suit becomes declarer's partner but does not reveal themselves until the king is played. Legal to call own king (play alone vs three).
customActions.constraints: Declarer only; in contracts that allow a partner (Rufer, Solo, Besserrufer).

customActions.description: Talon is shown in two sets of three. Declarer chooses one set, adds to hand, and discards three face-down into own tricks. Other set goes to opponents. Kings and Trull (Sküs, XXI, I) may never be discarded.
customActions.constraints: Declarer only; in contracts that allow talon exchange (Rufer, Sechserdreier, Besserrufer, Dreier, Farbendreier).

customActions.description: Declare a bonus (e.g. Pagat Ultimo, Trull, Valat) for double value, or say kontra/rekontra to double opponents' game or bonus. Round continues until three consecutive passes.
customActions.constraints: After talon exchange; declarer starts. Bonus announcements only if partner is known or you are declarer's partner.

customActions.description: Play a card of the suit led. Required if you hold that suit.
customActions.constraints: When you have at least one card of the led suit; must follow suit if possible.

customActions.description: Play a trump when you cannot follow suit. You must play a trump if you have no card of the led suit.
customActions.constraints: When you cannot follow suit; trumps beat any led suit (except in Farbensolo/Farbendreier).

customActions.description: Sum card points in tricks: each set of three cards sum values minus 2; one or two odd cards count one less than their total. Pack totals 70 points.
customActions.constraints: After all 12 tricks played; determines whether declarer made contract (36+ in positive).

customActions.description: Settle game points: losing side pays winning side the contract value; bonuses scored separately. In solo contracts declarer pays or is paid by each opponent.
customActions.constraints: After counting; applies solidarity of partnerships.

engine.deckDescription: A 54-card Industrie und Glück tarock deck with 21 numbered trumps plus the Skus and 32 suit cards. Black suits keep King, Queen, Cavalier, Jack, 10, 9, 8, 7; red suits keep King, Queen, Cavalier, Jack, Ace, 2, 3, 4.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits are divided into black suits (Spades and Clubs) and red suits (Hearts and Diamonds), each with its own reduced pip sequence.
engine.rankDescription: Courts are King, Queen, Cavalier, and Jack. Black suits continue with 10, 9, 8, 7; red suits continue with Ace, 2, 3, 4. Trumps run from 1 to 21 plus the Skus.
engine.dealPattern: Two packets of 6 cards each anticlockwise from dealer's right; 6 cards to talon after first packet.

scoring.description: Standard KÃ¶nigrufen scoring applies with RuÃŸbach-specific values for contracts and bonuses.
scoring.winCondition: In positive contracts declarer's side wins by taking at least 36 of 70 card points (plus talon share). In negative contracts win by losing every trick (Bettel), taking exactly one or two tricks (Piccolo/Zwiccolo), or taking fewest points (Trischaken). Bonuses (Trull, Pagat Ultimo, Valat, etc.) score game points independently.
